/-!
# Conjecture 2.81

by L. N. Shevrin

a) Does there exist an axiomatizable class of lattices $\mathfrak{K}$ such that the lattice
of all subsemigroups of a semigroup $S$ is isomorphic to some lattice in $\mathfrak{K}$ if and
only if $S$ is a free group?

b) The same question for free abelian groups.

Analogous questions have affirmative answers for torsion-free groups, for non-periodic
groups, for abelian torsion-free groups, for abelian non-periodic groups, for orderable
groups (the corresponding classes of lattices are even finitely axiomatizable). Thus, in the
posed questions one may assume from the outset that the semigroup $S$ is a torsion-free group
(respectively, a torsion-free abelian group).

## Formalisation notes

A class of lattices is *axiomatizable* if it is the class of all lattices satisfying some set
$T$ of first-order sentences. Lattices are regarded as ordered structures, so $T$ is a theory
in the first-order language `FirstOrder.Language.order` of a single binary relation `≤`,
interpreted in a lattice as the lattice order. Since `≤`, `⊔` and `⊓` are first-order
definable from each other, this gives the same axiomatizable classes of lattices as the
language with the two lattice operations.

The lattice of all subsemigroups of $S$ is `Subsemigroup S`, ordered by inclusion; its least
element is the empty subsemigroup. A lattice isomorphism is an order isomorphism `≃o`.
Semigroups are nonempty by convention, so `S` carries a `Nonempty` hypothesis.

"The semigroup $S$ is a free group" means that $S$ is isomorphic, as a semigroup, to
`FreeGroup X` for some type `X` of any cardinality; `X` may be empty, so the trivial group
counts as a free group. Similarly for free abelian groups, using
`Multiplicative (FreeAbelianGroup X)`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A lattice `L` is a model of the theory `T` in the language of orders, where the relation
symbol `≤` is interpreted as the lattice order of `L`. The lattices satisfying `T` form the
axiomatizable class of lattices with set of axioms `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.Model` together with `FirstOrder.Language.orderStructure` / `Language.order.OrderedStructure` (an alternative was to quantify over an explicit `Language.order.Structure L` with `OrderedStructure L` as a conjunct, which is equivalent but clutters the statement); `Theory.ModelType` (bundled models, but they carry no `Lattice` instance and Mathlib has no lattice theory in `Language.order`).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.81».IsLatticeModel
justification.why_needed: Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language.orderStructure` (interpreting the symbol `≤` of `Language.order` as the actual order) is deliberately not an instance, so `L ⊨ T` cannot be written directly for a `[Lattice L]`. `IsLatticeModel L T := letI := orderStructure L; L ⊨ T` packages this. The class 𝔎 axiomatized by T is then {lattices L | IsLatticeModel L T}. Two proved `@[category API]` lemmas accompany it: invariance under `≃o` (`IsLatticeModel.of_orderIso`) and the reduction `exists_orderIso_subsemigroup_iff` showing that 'Sub(S) is isomorphic to some lattice in 𝔎' is equivalent to `IsLatticeModel (Subsemigroup S) T`.

blocks.name: IsLatticeModel
blocks.text:
/-- A lattice `L` is a model of the theory `T` in the language of orders, where the relation
symbol `≤` is interpreted as the lattice order of `L`. The lattices satisfying `T` form the
axiomatizable class of lattices with set of axioms `T`. -/
def IsLatticeModel (L : Type*) [Lattice L] (T : Language.order.Theory) : Prop :=
  letI := orderStructure L
  L ⊨ T

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3 6]
theorem IsLatticeModel.of_orderIso {L L' : Type*} [Lattice L] [Lattice L'] (e : L ≃o L')
    {T : Language.order.Theory} (h : IsLatticeModel L T) : IsLatticeModel L' T := by
  unfold IsLatticeModel at *
  letI := orderStructure L
  letI := orderStructure L'
  haveI : Language.order.OrderedStructure L := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  haveI : Language.order.OrderedStructure L' := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  exact StrongHomClass.theory_model e

@[category API, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem exists_orderIso_subsemigroup_iff (S : Type) [Semigroup S]
    (T : Language.order.Theory) :
    (∃ (L : Type) (_ : Lattice L), IsLatticeModel L T ∧ Nonempty (Subsemigroup S ≃o L)) ↔
      IsLatticeModel (Subsemigroup S) T :=
  ⟨fun ⟨_, _, hL, ⟨e⟩⟩ => hL.of_orderIso e.symm, fun h => ⟨_, _, h, ⟨OrderIso.refl _⟩⟩⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: does there exist a class 𝔎 of lattices axiomatizable by a set of first-order sentences in the language of lattices (elementary class; the remark's 'even finitely axiomatizable' confirms the first-order reading, arbitrarily many axioms allowed) such that for EVERY semigroup S (any cardinality), the lattice Sub(S) of all subsemigroups (including the empty subsemigroup as bottom, as in Mathlib's `Subsemigroup S`) is lattice-isomorphic to a member of 𝔎 iff S is a free group, where 'S is a free group' means the semigroup S is (the multiplicative semigroup of) a group that is free on some set of any cardinality, including the trivial group (rank 0); the remark's known results mean one may equivalently restrict S to torsion-free groups, but this is a reformulation, not a separate question.
claims.reviewer_why: c07 states the question literally: ∃ first-order theory T (arbitrary set of sentences) in Mathlib's `Language.order`, ∀ semigroups S, (∃ lattice L ⊨ T with Subsemigroup S ≃o L) ↔ ∃ X, Nonempty (S ≃* FreeGroup X). It uses only Mathlib primitives plus one small bespoke def `IsLatticeModel` (packaging the non-instance `orderStructure`) with two API lemmas that prove the class is isomorphism-closed, so the literal 'isomorphic to some member of 𝔎' form and the direct 'Sub(S) ⊨ T' form (c03/c06) agree. `Subsemigroup S` has the empty subsemigroup as ⊥; X may be empty so the trivial group counts; MulEquiv onto a group forces S to be a group with the given multiplication. The {≤} signature gives the same elementary classes of lattices as {∨,∧}, so it is equivalent to the bespoke-language versions of c01/c04/c05/c06 while avoiding bespoke Language/Structure definitions. My edit: added `[Nonempty S]` (from c01) since semigroups are nonempty by convention; this is provably answer-neutral either way (Sub(∅) is the one-element lattice, which no nonempty semigroup has). Follows the repo's `Type` (universe 0) idiom used in the other Kourovka files.

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace Kourovka.«2.81»

/-- A lattice `L` is a model of the theory `T` in the language of orders, where the relation
symbol `≤` is interpreted as the lattice order of `L`. The lattices satisfying `T` form the
axiomatizable class of lattices with set of axioms `T`. -/
def IsLatticeModel (L : Type*) [Lattice L] (T : Language.order.Theory) : Prop :=
  letI := orderStructure L
  L ⊨ T

/-- Being a model of a theory in the language of orders is invariant under lattice
isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 6]
theorem IsLatticeModel.of_orderIso {L L' : Type*} [Lattice L] [Lattice L'] (e : L ≃o L')
    {T : Language.order.Theory} (h : IsLatticeModel L T) : IsLatticeModel L' T := by
  unfold IsLatticeModel at *
  letI := orderStructure L
  letI := orderStructure L'
  haveI : Language.order.OrderedStructure L := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  haveI : Language.order.OrderedStructure L' := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  exact StrongHomClass.theory_model e

/-- The lattice of all subsemigroups of `S` is isomorphic to some lattice in the axiomatizable
class of lattices with set of axioms `T` if and only if it is itself a model of `T`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem exists_orderIso_subsemigroup_iff (S : Type) [Semigroup S]
    (T : Language.order.Theory) :
    (∃ (L : Type) (_ : Lattice L), IsLatticeModel L T ∧ Nonempty (Subsemigroup S ≃o L)) ↔
      IsLatticeModel (Subsemigroup S) T :=
  ⟨fun ⟨_, _, hL, ⟨e⟩⟩ => hL.of_orderIso e.symm, fun h => ⟨_, _, h, ⟨OrderIso.refl _⟩⟩⟩

/--
a) Does there exist an axiomatizable class of lattices $\mathfrak{K}$ such that the lattice
of all subsemigroups of a semigroup $S$ is isomorphic to some lattice in $\mathfrak{K}$ if and
only if $S$ is a free group?

Here $\mathfrak{K}$ is the class of all lattices that are models of a set $T$ of first-order
sentences in the language of orders, and "$S$ is a free group" means that the semigroup $S$ is
isomorphic (as a semigroup) to a free group on some set $X$; the trivial group (the case
$X = \varnothing$) is included.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.81».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ T : Language.order.Theory, ∀ (S : Type) [Semigroup S] [Nonempty S],
      (∃ (L : Type) (_ : Lattice L), IsLatticeModel L T ∧ Nonempty (Subsemigroup S ≃o L)) ↔
        ∃ X : Type, Nonempty (S ≃* FreeGroup X) := by
  sorry

/--
b) Does there exist an axiomatizable class of lattices $\mathfrak{K}$ such that the lattice
of all subsemigroups of a semigroup $S$ is isomorphic to some lattice in $\mathfrak{K}$ if and
only if $S$ is a free abelian group?

Here $\mathfrak{K}$ is the class of all lattices that are models of a set $T$ of first-order
sentences in the language of orders, and "$S$ is a free abelian group" means that the semigroup
$S$ is isomorphic (as a semigroup) to a free abelian group on some set $X$; the trivial group
(the case $X = \varnothing$) is included.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.81».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ T : Language.order.Theory, ∀ (S : Type) [Semigroup S] [Nonempty S],
      (∃ (L : Type) (_ : Lattice L), IsLatticeModel L T ∧ Nonempty (Subsemigroup S ≃o L)) ↔
        ∃ X : Type, Nonempty (S ≃* Multiplicative (FreeAbelianGroup X)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.81»

items: Language of lattices: lattices are treated as ordered structures and T is a theory in Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language.order` (single binary relation ≤ interpreted as the lattice order), rather than the signature {∨, ∧}. Since ≤ is definable from ∨ (x ≤ y ↔ x ∨ y = y) and ∨, ∧ are first-order definable from ≤, the two signatures yield exactly the same axiomatizable classes of lattices, so the question is unchanged. Arbitrary (possibly infinite) sets of axioms are allowed, per the notes.

'Isomorphic to some lattice in 𝔎' is kept literally as `∃ (L : Type) (_ : Lattice L), IsLatticeModel L T ∧ Nonempty (Subsemigroup S ≃o L)`; the API lemma `exists_orderIso_subsemigroup_iff` proves it is equivalent to `IsLatticeModel (Subsemigroup S) T`, so restricting L to `Type` (same universe as `Subsemigroup S`) loses nothing.

Semigroups S range over `Type` (universe 0), following the Kourovka files' idiom (`∀ (G : Type) [Group G]`). Mathlib's `Semigroup` does not require nonemptiness, so the empty semigroup is included; this does not affect the answer: Sub(∅) is the one-element lattice, no group has a one-element subsemigroup lattice, and the singleton lattice can be excluded from any candidate class by the single axiom ∃x∃y, x ≠ y.

'S is a free group' for a semigroup S is formalized as `∃ X : Type, Nonempty (S ≃* FreeGroup X)`: a multiplicative bijection from S onto a free group, i.e. the multiplicative semigroup of S is a free group. The trivial group (X = Empty) is included, as the notes require. Since S : Type, bases X : Type suffice for every cardinality of free group in that universe.

'S is a free abelian group' is `∃ X : Type, Nonempty (S ≃* Multiplicative (FreeAbelianGroup X))`, using Mathlib's additive `FreeAbelianGroup` made multiplicative to match the semigroup S; trivial group included.

`Subsemigroup S` is Mathlib's complete lattice of subsemigroups ordered by inclusion, whose ⊥ is the empty subsemigroup (checked: `((⊥ : Subsemigroup S) : Set S) = ∅` by `rfl`), matching the notes and Shevrin's convention. `≃o` between lattices is lattice isomorphism.
The remark's known results (torsion-free groups etc.) are treated as background/reformulation, not separate slots, and are recorded only in the module docstring.
AMS tags 3 (logic/model theory), 6 (lattices), 20 (group theory) are used for both slots.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates formalized both slots and all compiled; none omitted a slot, and the differences are only in equivalent modeling choices: (1) signature for the lattice language — Mathlib `Language.order` (c02,c03,c07,c08) vs a bespoke {⊔,⊓} language (c01,c04,c05,c06); these yield identical axiomatizable classes of lattices since ≤ and ⊔,⊓ are mutually first-order definable; (2) literal 'isomorphic to some L ∈ 𝔎' (c01,c02,c04,c05,c07,c08) vs direct 'Subsemigroup S ⊨ T' (c03,c06), equivalent because elementary classes are isomorphism-closed (c07's API lemma proves this in Lean); (3) `Type` vs `Type u` for S — both acceptable, `Type` matches the existing Kourovka files; (4) presence of `[Nonempty S]` (only c01) — answer-neutral, but included in the final file as the literal rendering of 'semigroup'. c04's `IsFreeGroupSemigroup` (∃ group structure with the same semigroup reduct that is `IsFreeGroup`) is equivalent to the MulEquiv encoding but heavier. c05/c06 tag only AMS 20; final file uses AMS 3 6 20. Ambiguity in the source: 'axiomatizable' read as first-order axiomatizable by an arbitrary set of sentences (the remark's 'even finitely axiomatizable' confirms the first-order reading); the remark's reduction to torsion-free (abelian) groups is treated as a reformulation and only recorded in the module docstring, per the decomposition table. Final file compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
